title: Tomorrow: three meetings, a dentist appointment, and a 4-hour focus block
summary: A constraint-first schedule that exposes the missing uninterrupted four-hour window.

blocks.heading: Four hours fit. One four-hour block does not.
blocks.body: Fictional day, matching the paired agenda: meetings at 08:30–09:00, 11:15–12:00 and 14:15–14:45; dentist 13:00–13:45; work ends 17:10. The existing plan offers 09:05–11:05 and 14:50–16:50. That is four hours total in two pieces.

blocks.heading: Keep these anchors unless the other person agrees
rows: Lunch and 20 min outbound travel before dentist
blocks.caption: Same fictional appointments as the paired agenda. Travel, lunch and transitions are real claims on the day.

slides.title: Keep all appointments
slides.body: Reserve 09:05–11:05 and 14:50–16:50 for the same focus task. You get four hours of work, with a midday interruption. Leave a restart note before lunch.

slides.title: Require one uninterrupted block
slides.body: Ask to move both the 13:00 dentist appointment and the 14:15 1:1 to another day. If both moves are confirmed, take lunch 12:00–12:30 and focus 12:30–16:30. Until then, this option is not available.

slides.title: Keep the appointments and shorten the day
slides.body: Protect one two-hour focus session and reschedule the remaining work. Reduce the deliverable explicitly; do not pretend the original four-hour task still fits.

blocks.heading: Check the constraint
blocks.prompt: Moving only the 14:15 meeting leaves the dentist fixed. Does that create a four-hour afternoon block before 17:10?
blocks.explanation: After the appointment and return travel, the afternoon starts around 14:15, leaving under three hours. The dentist remains an anchor.

blocks.title: Schedule options, not a calendar editor
blocks.body: Use the arrows to compare plans. This page cannot drag blocks, change appointments or save a schedule. Confirm any move with the people involved before relying on it.
